import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1105

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1105](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1105)
- [ESS75] Erdős, P. and Simonovits, M. and Sós, V. T., Anti-{R}amsey theorems. (1975), 633--643.
- [MoNe05] Montellano-Ballesteros, J. J. and Neumann-Lara, V., An anti-{R}amsey theorem on cycles.
  Graphs Combin. (2005), 343--354.
- [SiSo84] Simonovits, Miklós and Sós, Vera T., On restricted colourings of {$K_n$}. Combinatorica
  (1984), 101--110.
- [Yu21] L.-T. Yuan, The anti-Ramsey number for paths. arXiv:2102.00807 (2021).
-/

namespace Erdos1105

open SimpleGraph Asymptotics Filter

/--
The anti-Ramsey number $\mathrm{AR}(n,G)$ is the maximum possible number of colours in which the
edges of $K_n$ can be coloured without creating a rainbow copy of $G$ (i.e. one in which all edges
have different colours).

Let $C_k$ be the cycle on $k$ vertices. Is it true that
$\mathrm{AR}(n,C_k)=\left(\frac{k-2}{2}+\frac{1}{k-1}\right)n+O(1)$?

Montellano-Ballesteros and Neumann-Lara [MoNe05] gave an exact formula for $\mathrm{AR}(n,C_k)$,
which implies in particular that
$\mathrm{AR}(n,C_k)=\left(\frac{k-2}{2}+\frac{1}{k-1}\right)n+O(1).$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1105.parts.i : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ k, 3 ≤ k →
    ((fun n => (antiRamseyNum (cycleGraph k) n : ℝ) - ((k - 2 : ℝ) / 2 + 1 / (k - 1)) * n)
      =O[atTop] (fun _ => (1 : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $P_k$ be the path on $k$ vertices and $\ell=\lfloor\frac{k-1}{2}\rfloor$. If $n\geq k\geq 5$
then is $\mathrm{AR}(n,P_k)$ equal to $\max\left(\binom{k-2}{2}+1,
\binom{\ell-1}{2}+(\ell-1)(n-\ell+1)+\epsilon\right)$where $\epsilon=1$ if $k$ is odd and
$\epsilon=2$ otherwise?

A proof of the formula for $\mathrm{AR}(n,P_k)$ for all $n\geq k\geq 5$ has been announced by
Yuan [Yu21].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1105.parts.ii : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (k n : ℕ), 5 ≤ k → k ≤ n →
    let ℓ := (k - 1) / 2
    let ε := if Odd k then 1 else 2
    antiRamseyNum (pathGraph k) n = max ((k - 2).choose 2 + 1) ((ℓ - 1).choose 2 +
      (ℓ - 1) * (n - ℓ + 1) + ε) := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add Erdős, Simonovits, and Sós variant.
-- TODO: Add Simonovits and Sós variant.

end Erdos1105

findings.description: The shared definition used by both Erdos1105.erdos_1105.parts.i and Erdos1105.erdos_1105.parts.ii counts colors on diagonal pairs. It maximizes over surjective c : Sym2 (Fin n) → Fin k, but Sym2 includes all n pairs {v,v}, which are not edges of K_n. These pairs can receive fresh colors without affecting IsRainbow. This makes both reviewed formulas false. For C₃, coloring actual edges by their minimum endpoint and assigning fresh diagonal colors gives antiRamseyNum(C₃,n) ≥ 2n−1, so the difference from the claimed leading term n is unbounded. For k=n=5 in part ii, monochromatic actual edges plus five distinct diagonal colors give antiRamseyNum(P₅,5) ≥ 6, whereas the formula evaluates to 5. Both contradictions were proved in the scratch Lean file without using sorry axioms.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős–Simonovits–Sós, Anti-Ramsey theorems (1975), p.633, defines the maximum using colors of the edges of K_n and explicitly says graphs have no loops or multiple edges; Appendix A, p.642, proves f(n,C₃)=n−1. https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-05.pdf . Yuan's introduction and Theorem 1 use the same edge-coloring definition and give AR(5,P₅)=5: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2102.00807 . Both claims are restated at https://www.erdosproblems.com/1105 .
findings.suggested_fix: Change the coloring domain to (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet and evaluate colors on homomorphism edge images using Hom.mapEdgeSet. Alternatively, retain the full Sym2 coloring but require surjectivity only of its restriction to the actual edge subtype. The separate copy-versus-homomorphism defect must also be repaired. Keep the source formulas and affirmative answers.

findings.description: The condition ∀ f : H →g ⊤, ¬IsRainbow f c forbids arbitrary rainbow homomorphisms, not rainbow copies. IsRainbow requires injectivity only on edge colors, which does not force injectivity on vertices. For example, on K₅ give the four edges incident with vertex 4 distinct colors and all other edges a fifth color. There is no rainbow P₅ copy, but the noninjective map [4,0,1,4,2] is a rainbow P₅ homomorphism. This changes the extremal number independently of the diagonal defect: after restricting to actual edges, any five colors on K₅ supply five representative edges; every five-edge graph on five vertices has a four-edge trail, yielding a rainbow P₅ homomorphism. Thus that variant has at most four colors, rather than the source's five. The coloring witness and the finite trail assertion were verified in Lean. An analogous C₆ example—two rainbow triangles sharing a vertex inside a rainbow K₅ in K₆—also verifies that the cycle avoidance predicate is different.
findings.source_evidence: ESS75, p.633, excludes a rainbow subgraph 'isomorphic to H', not a homomorphic image: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-05.pdf . Simonovits–Sós likewise specifies 'subgraphs isomorphic to H' and simple graphs on p.101: https://www.renyi.hu/~miki/sos50RestrictedCCA.pdf . Yuan's introduction explicitly gives the star-based P₅-free coloring above, and Theorem 1 gives AR(5,P₅)=5: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2102.00807 .
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the forbidden maps to injective homomorphisms: use ∀ f : H →g ⊤, Function.Injective f → ¬IsRainbow f c, or quantify over SimpleGraph.Copy H (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)). With the actual-edge coloring domain, the rainbow test can be ¬ Function.Injective (fun e : H.edgeSet => c (f.toHom.mapEdgeSet e)). Do not replace homomorphisms with ↪g, which would require induced copies. A corrected definition using edgeSet and Copy typechecks in the scratch file.

namespace Erdos1105

open SimpleGraph Asymptotics Filter

/--
The maximum number of colours used on the edges of $K_n$ in a colouring with no rainbow copy of $H$.
-/
private noncomputable def antiRamseyNumber {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
    (H : SimpleGraph α) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {r | ∃ c : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet → Fin r,
    Function.Surjective c ∧
    ∀ f : Copy H (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      ¬ Function.Injective (fun e : H.edgeSet => c (f.toHom.mapEdgeSet e))}
